reason: The cited evidence (E1) demonstrates TiO precipitate formation and associated strengthening in a different refractory HEA (NbMoTaWVTi) processed by MA and SPS, but it does not provide any data on high-temperature mechanical properties, grain boundary stabilization, or behavior of the TiVNbTa system. The key premises about high-temperature effectiveness, applicability to TiVNbTa, and matrix integrity are therefore unsupported by the cited passage.
premises: TiO precipitates can form in a refractory high-entropy alloy matrix via controlled processing
TiO precipitates act as effective obstacles to dislocation motion at high temperature
TiO precipitates stabilize grain boundaries against high-temperature softening
Precipitation strengthening from TiO can overcome the strength drop observed in TiVNbTa at 1273 K
The processing route (oxygen addition) will produce a fine, uniform dispersion of TiO without degrading the BCC matrix
